en.title: Resident Evil 4 Remake Leak Reveals Original Plan to Connect to Village
en.summary: Over 600 unused voice lines discovered in the Resident Evil 4 Remake launch disc hint at a deeper connection to the series' eighth installment, Village. A leaked line from the Merchant directly references 'The Duke,' suggesting a more intertwined narrative that was ultimately cut.
en.body:
The depths of **Resident Evil 4 Remake**'s launch disc have yielded a trove of over 600 unused voice lines, with one particular snippet suggesting a more direct narrative link to **Resident Evil Village** than fans ever knew. Modder Keff0 unearthed these fully recorded lines, featuring main characters like Leon, Luis, Ashley, and the enigmatic Merchant, all of which were absent from the final game and the PC version. These discoveries paint a picture of Capcom's initial ambitions for interconnected storytelling within the modern **Resident Evil** era.

One of the most striking revelations comes from the Merchant himself. In an unearthed line, he remarks, "Ah, I see you’re no stranger to villages. The Duke? Lad shows promise." This direct reference to **The Duke**, the beloved merchant character from **Resident Evil Village**, implies a deliberate attempt by the developers to tie the two games together narratively. In **Village**, players will recall The Duke referencing the **Resident Evil 4** merchant with his own iconic catchphrase, "What’re ya buyin’?" – "just something an old friend of mine used to say." The cut line from the **RE4 Remake** Merchant would have retroactively strengthened this connection, adding a layer of continuity that was ultimately omitted from the released product.

## Echoes of The Duke

The existence of this dialogue raises intriguing questions about Capcom's development process and their overarching vision for the **Resident Evil** series. While the **Resident Evil 4 Remake** is a masterful reimagining of a classic, the decision to cut a line that so explicitly bridges the gap to **Village** is noteworthy. The developers might have considered that such a direct mention could be jarring for players unfamiliar with **Village**, or perhaps they simply wanted **Resident Evil 4 Remake** to stand more firmly on its own. The **Resident Evil** franchise has a long history of both interconnected lore and standalone entries, and this cut content highlights the delicate balance Capcom must strike when weaving its complex universe together.

## Fan Reactions and Future Implications

For passionate fans who devour every detail of the **Resident Evil** lore, this leak is a compelling piece of evidence for a more unified narrative direction that was considered. It fuels speculation about how future **Resident Evil** titles might continue to cross-pollinate characters and plot threads. While Capcom has confirmed that the VR version of **Resident Evil 4 Remake** did alter some dialogue, they have also stated that such leaks do not indicate future game releases. This discovery, however, serves as a fascinating post-script to the game's development, offering a tantalizing 'what if' scenario for fans who appreciate the intricate tapestry of the **Resident Evil** universe.

## What's Next

Capcom has previously taken a firm stance against leaks, citing copyright infringement and the potential to spoil excitement for other players. While no new game announcements are directly tied to this voice line leak, the **Resident Evil** franchise continues to be a cornerstone of survival horror. Fans will undoubtedly be keeping a close watch for any official word on future installments or potential narrative expansions that might explore these connections further.

content_raw: Ovee 30 minutes’ worth of unused voice lines from Resident Evil 4 Remake have surfaced online, one of which proves that Capcom wanted to make a connection to Village. This leak comes from a notable community modder named Keff0, who uncovered both audio and subtitles for a whopping 671 lines on the game’s PlayStation 5 launch disc. These lines aren’t on the PC version of the game, and they’re fully recorded, featuring dialogue from Leon, Luis, Ashley, and the Merchant. One of the Merchant’s unused lines is standing out to viewers, as he mentions a character that wasn’t even a blink in the RE Team’s mind when the game was first made back in the mid-2000s. “Ah, I see you’re no stranger to villages. The Duke? Lad shows promise,” the Merchant says. Resident Evil fans will make the connection to the series’ eighth game, Village, which features another merchant character who simply calls himself ‘The Duke.’ Funny enough, The Duke also references the Resident Evil 4 merchant as players browse through his wares, saying, “‘What’re ya buyin’?’ Haha, just something an old friend of mine used to say.” Capcom’s decision to cut The Merchant’s line from RE4 Remake is a bit saddening, as it would have further cemented the relationship between these characters and added a bit more continuity to the timeline, if retroactively. However, this insertion of a modern-day Resident Evil character in the series’ single-most beloved game could have rubbed some players the wrong way, though we’ll never know for certain why Capcom chose to leave this particular dialogue out of the final product. 😮Over 600 cut voice lines have been found in Resident Evil 4 Remake. Modder Keff0, who previously restored the game’s cut Chapter 0 and made it playable, has now uncovered 671 finished voice lines that were cut from Resident Evil 4 Remake. 🔎All of the lines can be found on… pic.twitter.com/obSogcJG6t — RENEWS (@RENews_X) September 1, 2026 This wasn’t the only interesting find from the RE4 Remake; Keff0 also uncovered unused animations for the Merchant’s death, meaning that originally, players would have been able kill him. His shop was even supposed to close after he died, and save data found by Keff0 shows that he’d be gone for the rest of the game. This would have made it more similar to the original, but it seems like the team at Capcom thought that’d be too counterintuitive to this modern rework of the title. Like many AAA games, there’s a swath of unused lines, scenes, art, enemies, characters, and other assets in recent Resident Evil titles that don’t make it to the final cut; earlier this year, Leon’s voice actor revealed that his favorite line in Resident Evil Requiem was ultimately axed by Capcom — and it’s a shame, because it was hilarious. Luckily, there’s much more to come, with Code Veronica getting a remake in 2027 and a live-action Resident Evil movie directed by Zach Cregger set to hit theaters this month.
